newsitem.title: CHILE: Drought seen draining Chilean shares.
newsitem.headline: Drought seen draining Chilean shares.

text.p: Chilean blue chips were expected to trade mixed to lower Friday as concerns that drought will cut profits in the electrical sector continued to trouble the market.
''The market remains very depressed about the drought's effects on the electricals but other industries are all right,'' said one broker.
The blue-chip IPSA index ended a full percentage point lower on Thursday at 116.72 points, dragged down by heavy-volume electrical shares like Enersis and Chilgener.

Chilgener's general manager Juan Antonio Guzman said on local television Thursday that electricity rationing may be necessary now, rather than early next month as foreseen by the government, because of a sharp drop in water levels at hydroelectric dams.
Chile depends on hydro power for about 70 percent of its energy needs. Severe drought in the country's central heartland has dried up reservoirs and turned rivers into mere trickles.
This week's series of Central Bank announcements liberalizing access to foreign currency markets for Chilean overseas investors was seen as having little net impact on the market, brokers said.
